This normalizer is copy-pasted across packages (anthropic x3 `_to_lists`, langchain `_normalize_tuples_to_lists`, smolagents `_normalize_span_value`). Unit tests also only compare against hand-written literals or spot-check a field, so a missing required field (e.g. `parts`) still passes. What about one shared helper in `test_util_genai` that unit tests use to read content attributes? It would check the exact type and validate against the pinned semconv schemas:

```python
# util/opentelemetry-test-util-genai/src/opentelemetry/test_util_genai/content.py
from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

import jsonschema

from opentelemetry.test_util_genai._setup_weaver import _provision_genai_root

_SCHEMA_FILES = {
    "gen_ai.input.messages": "gen-ai-input-messages.json",
    "gen_ai.output.messages": "gen-ai-output-messages.json",
    "gen_ai.system_instructions": "gen-ai-system-instructions.json",
    "gen_ai.tool.definitions": "gen-ai-tool-definitions.json",
    "gen_ai.retrieval.documents": "gen-ai-retrieval-documents.json",
}


@functools.cache
def _validator(name: str) -> jsonschema.Draft202012Validator:
    path = _provision_genai_root() / "model" / "gen-ai" / _SCHEMA_FILES[name]
    return jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


def _to_json_like(value: Any, path: str) -> Any:
    # SDK attributes store sequences as tuples; anything else (list, JSON string,
    # dataclass) means the value wasn't converted to AnyValue.
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [_to_json_like(v, f"{path}[{i}]") for i, v in enumerate(value)]
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        return {k: _to_json_like(v, f"{path}.{k}") for k, v in value.items()}
    assert value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int, float, bytes)), (
        f"{path}: unexpected {type(value).__name__}"
    )
    return value


def get_content_attribute(attributes: Mapping[str, Any], name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return a structured GenAI content attribute as plain lists/dicts.

    Asserts the value is a structured sequence and matches the semconv JSON schema.
    """
    value = attributes[name]
    assert isinstance(value, tuple), f"{name}: expected tuple, got {type(value).__name__}"
    normalized = _to_json_like(value, name)
    errors = [e.message for e in _validator(name).iter_errors(normalized)]
    assert not errors, f"{name} does not match the semconv schema: {errors}"
    return normalized
```

Then the per-package helpers become `get_content_attribute(span.attributes, GenAI.GEN_AI_INPUT_MESSAGES)`, and `jsonschema` moves from `dev-requirements-conformance.txt` to the shared test deps. The schema download is pinned via `versions.env` and cached under `SEMCONV_CACHE`, so it happens once per env.

threads.body: Two valid calls to the same tool can have identical scalar attributes but different structured arguments, so both match the same report sample. This assertion then aborts conformance even though the telemetry is valid. Correlate samples with captured spans using stable trace/span identifiers, preserving those in the report if necessary, rather than requiring matching spans to have identical payloads.

replies.body: Weaver's `SampleSpan` JSON output does not preserve `trace_id` or `span_id` (unlike `SampleLog`), and `execute_tool` spans carry distinct `gen_ai.tool.call.id` scalar attributes. This enrichment helper is also a temporary bridge until upstream Weaver supports `KvlistValue` directly (https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/pull/1873).

threads.body: Since weaver drops maps, nothing validates structured content against the schema until open-telemetry/weaver#1873 ships - e.g. the anthropic multimodal scenario passes with `bytes` blob content that the schema rejects. This re-hydration only feeds hand-written scenario asserts that unit tests already cover via `get_content_attribute`. What about dropping it (plus the in-memory exporters) and skipping the content checks in scenarios until the weaver bump?
